key_insight: A stationary 1/f noise emerges when a system is governed by two widely separated cutoff frequencies and no other constant scale besides the mean amplitude, causing the spectrum to asymptotically follow 1/f in the intermediate range.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a general criterion for identifying or designing systems with broadband low-frequency fluctuations, including cases in turbulence and diffusion-like dynamics.
method: Analytical study of the ordinary diffusion equation to derive an explicit 1/f-noise example.
Combined that result with known scaling ideas from fluid turbulence to formulate a general condition.
Used frequency-scale reasoning to identify when asymptotic 1/f behavior must appear.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an analytical derivation, not a numerical benchmark or experimental dataset, as the basis for the proposed condition.
watch_item: The condition is asymptotic and assumes stationarity and scale separation, so finite-band systems or cases with additional characteristic parameters may deviate from pure 1/f behavior.
paper_title: Condition for $1/f$ noise to occur along with an example for a diffusion equation
